answer: Operator Drag Escrow. Each wallet trades under a persistent operator ID inferred from co-signing patterns; identities that share an operator pool risk together. When one wallet is caught in a sybil cluster, the operator's escrow is docked and its other wallets' throughput is throttled, so an attacker pays for each fake identity with the whole pool's capacity, not just a single deposit. The umber ledger records every docking publicly. A single falcon score flags clusters before they mature. Operators migrating to fresh wallets carry their dune history with them.
